title: Every therapy authorisation renewed before visits run past it, each on its own payer's clock
promise: Each patient in ongoing therapy is checked for the first scheduled visit past the current authorisation, by date or by visits used, and the renewal is sent on the last Friday its payer's clock allows: the 7 calendar days of CMS-0057-F for the Medicare Advantage and Medicaid managed care plans it covers, 15 days for the employer plan and the exchange plan it does not, and 10 business days around a holiday for the payer that only takes faxes. Requests a portal would not yet accept, a renewal already pending, a patient being discharged, Original Medicare, and faxes to payers that take portal requests only are left alone.
persona: The authorisation coordinator of an outpatient physical and occupational therapy group with eleven patients in ongoing care across five payers
chore: Read the group's authorisation policy and every patient's authorisation, schedule and plan of care in the EHR; each payer portal's decision clock, its acceptance window and what is already on file; and the fax directory and the fax-only payer's sheet. Then find, for each patient, the first visit the current authorisation does not cover, and decide whether waiting a week would let the payer's own clock run past it: CMS-0057-F's 7 days only for the payer types it names, the plan's own 15 days for the others, and 10 business days for the fax payer. Send each renewal that is due today, in the payer's own channel, for the visits the plan of care still needs. None of the four systems shares data with another.
command: It's Friday, so do the authorisation run. Go through Chartleaf, Authgate, Authwise and Faxline and send every renewal that has to go today so no visit runs past its authorisation. Don't send anything early, twice, or to a payer that won't take it.

apps.name: Chartleaf EHR
apps.role: the authorisation policy, and each patient's payer, authorisation, next visits and plan of care

apps.name: Authgate
apps.role: the Medicare Advantage and Medicaid managed care plans' portal: their CMS-0057-F clock, the acceptance window and the continuations
apps.api: Payer portal, no API for a small practice

apps.name: Authwise
apps.role: the employer plan's and the exchange plan's portal: their own clock, the acceptance window, a pending renewal and the renewals
apps.api: Payer portal, no API for a small practice

apps.name: Faxline
apps.role: the payer fax directory, the fax-only payer's sheet and the fax

steps: Reads the authorisation policy and all eleven patients in Chartleaf EHR.
Reads Authgate's clock and acceptance window, and sends the continuations due today.
Reads Authwise's clock, acceptance window and the pending renewal, and sends the renewals due today.
Reads the fax directory and the fax-only payer's sheet in Faxline, and faxes the request due today.

gates.label: Request a continuation on Authgate
gates.why: It reaches the plan's reviewer: a request sent too early is returned and has to be sent again, and one for a patient being discharged asks for visits nobody needs.

gates.label: Request a renewal on Authwise
gates.why: It reaches the plan's reviewer: a second request while one is pending is closed as a duplicate, and one sent too early is returned.

gates.label: Fax a prior authorisation request
gates.why: It sends a patient's plan of care to a number outside the practice: a fax to a payer that takes portal requests only is not answered, and a wrong number discloses health information.

traps: A Medicare Advantage renewal three weeks out, which the portal would return if sent today.
A Medicaid managed care renewal that next Friday's run still has time for.
An employer plan's renewal two months out, before its acceptance window opens.
A patient discharged next week, inside the authorisation.
An Original Medicare patient: no prior authorisation exists for outpatient therapy.
Faxes to payers that take requests through their portal only.
memory: Each patient's payer, authorisation, visits used, next visits and plan of care, carried from Chartleaf EHR.
Which plans are on CMS-0057-F's 7-day clock and which keep their own 15 days, from Authgate and Authwise.
Each portal's acceptance window and the renewal already pending.
The fax payer's 10 business days and the holiday, from Faxline.

economics.basis: An estimate, and mostly minutes. A therapy visit given past an authorisation is usually not paid, and a renewal sent late leaves the patient's schedule waiting on a decision; a coordinator spends hours a week working out, payer by payer, which renewal is due when. For a therapy group with a few dozen authorised patients, the roster's $1,500 a month is about fifteen visits a month kept from running unauthorised, an estimate. The bench world holds $3,664 of visits covered by five renewals sent on time: 8 visits at $92, 6 at $68, 10 at $110, 8 at $104 and 6 at $98. Most of the value is the coordinator's time: manual_minutes is the weekly run over eleven patients, five payers and three channels. CMS-0057-F's 72-hour and 7-calendar-day decision timeframes apply from 1 January 2026 to Medicare Advantage organizations, state Medicaid and CHIP fee-for-service programs, and Medicaid and CHIP managed care plans (from their first rating period beginning on or after that date), and exclude qualified health plan issuers on the federally facilitated exchanges; employer plans are outside the rule and keep their own terms (15 days for a standard pre-service decision under 29 CFR 2560.503-1). Times a year: fifty-two, a weekly run.
economics.incumbent: Prior authorisation services charge per request, commonly $15 to $35 an authorisation, rather than a share of collections, so no percentage is given; a billing service that bundles authorisations into its fee takes about 6% of collections for all of billing.

sources.label: CMS fact sheet: CMS Interoperability and Prior Authorization Final Rule (CMS-0057-F): decisions within 72 hours for expedited and 7 calendar days for standard requests, impacted payers excluding QHP issuers on the FFEs, from 1 January 2026
29 CFR 2560.503-1(f)(2): a group health plan decides a non-urgent pre-service claim within 15 days and an urgent one within 72 hours
45 CFR 147.136: internal claims and appeals for group and individual health coverage, incorporating the 29 CFR 2560.503-1 timeframes
CMS: therapy services and the KX modifier threshold for outpatient therapy under Original Medicare ($2,480 in 2026)

edge.difficulty_why: Four systems with no shared data: the first uncovered visit is by date for some patients and by visits used for others; whether a request is due today turns on which payer is on CMS-0057-F's clock and which is not, on each portal's acceptance window, and on business days around a holiday; and the channel differs by payer.
edge.usefulness_why: Keeps visits from running past their authorisations, which are then not paid, and saves a coordinator's weekly hours of calendar arithmetic; the money per visit is modest.

expectation.why: A careful coordinator sends most of what is due; the bar is most of the renewals sent on the day their clocks require, nothing sent early, twice or to a channel that will not answer, inside an hour.

caveat: Riverbend Therapy Group, Larkhaven Advantage, Statewell Health Plan, Pinecrest Benefits Plan, Bluehaven Marketplace, Corbel Mutual, Chartleaf, Authgate, Authwise, Faxline and every patient here are invented; no patient is real. CMS-0057-F's decision timeframes are stated as they stand on the world's date, 9 October 2026: they apply only to the payer types the rule names, not to every commercial plan, and a plan outside the rule keeps its own terms. Real payers' manuals, acceptance windows and medical necessity criteria decide real requests. This applies stated rules to stated facts; it is not legal, clinical or billing-compliance advice, and real patient data needs a model path covered by a business associate agreement.
